scope: Retire NGE expertise, item, buff, cybernetic proc, cybernetic special-command, movement-buff, combat-modifier, reactive combat-proc runtime, generic proc-buff admission, both direct proc/reaction add-side effect writers, and all direct proc combat-action entry points for players while preserving Publish 14.1 combat authority, retained proc/item/cybernetic data and objects, removal cleanup, and expansion NPC encounter mechanics.

findings: The pinned Publish 14.1 combat runtime has no NGE expertise, item-proc, cybernetic-proc, or reactive-proc list authority.
The inherited login, weapon, wearable, buff, and cybernetic callbacks rebuild later-era proc lists even after NGE expertise and class admission are retired.
Authenticated PRE-CU combat already bypasses proc execution, but persisted lists and retained unprofiled commands leave a player-runtime reachability gap.
The shared expertise cache helper is reached directly by player login and delayed buff callbacks, so the downstream proc builders alone did not prevent a transient NGE expertise-proc list write.

Seven retained expansion cybernetic rows directly grant seven NGE combat commands on equip; the pinned Publish 14.1 runtime has none of those commands, and retained item data must not become player combat authority.

The retained cybernetic helper also exposed one permanent movement buff plus eight later combat-modifier writers and consumers. Its login validator removed those modifiers and immediately re-granted them from equipped items, so command/proc retirement alone did not close cybernetic player gameplay authority.

The retained proc table contains 97 rows and 96 distinct queued combat commands, while 72 retained buff rows carry proc_buff or reac_buff effect parameters. The normal player proc engine was already fail-closed, but generic buff admission and direct command dispatch remained alternate entry points.

All 96 proc commands have retained command, combat-data, and combat-action handlers. Ninety-five handlers use combatStandardAction; expertise_fs_flurry_charge_proc bypasses that shared path and therefore requires its own player-only guard.

The generic proc_buff and reac_buff admission and list builders were already player-inert, but procBuffAddBuffHandler and reactiveBuffAddBuffHandler could still be invoked directly and wrote procBuffEffects or reacBuffEffects before rebuilding later-era lists. Both add-side writers now invoke central player proc cleanup and return before parsing or mutation; their remove halves remain available for cleanup and non-player expansion behavior is unchanged.
